Quarantine

/KWAR-un-teen/ — rhymes with green · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To quarantine someone or something is to keep them isolated from others for a period of time so that an illness cannot spread.

The new parrot spent two weeks in quarantine before joining the aviary.

Worked Example

The hospital quarantined the patient suspected of carrying a highly contagious disease to prevent the virus from spreading to staff and other patients.

Quarantine is precise because it emphasizes both the isolation AND the specific reason — disease prevention. Plain 'isolated' would miss the health-control aspect. 'Quarantine' is the exact term for this specific medical practice of preventing disease spread.

How Quarantine Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

isolate

isolate: to set someone completely apart from others

confine

confine: to keep within limits or an enclosed space

segregate

segregate: to separate one group from all others

Antonyms

integrate

integrate: to bring someone back into the group

reunite

reunite: to bring separated people back together again

How Strong Is It? — separate → isolate → quarantine → imprison

separate vs. quarantine

separate vs. quarantine: Separate is far weaker than quarantine: separated things are simply kept apart, while quarantine enforces strict isolation for a set time to stop illness from spreading.

isolate vs. quarantine

isolate vs. quarantine: Isolate is weaker than quarantine — isolating sets someone apart, but quarantine adds official rules, a fixed time period, and the specific goal of containing disease.

imprison vs. quarantine

imprison vs. quarantine: Imprison is stronger than quarantine: quarantine confines someone temporarily for everyone's protection, while imprisoning locks a person away as punishment and strips their freedom entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — quaranta

Root — quaranta: forty (Italian)

Put it together

Put it together: Quarantine comes from Italian quaranta, 'forty' - Venice made ships from plague-stricken ports wait quaranta giorni, forty days, offshore before anyone could land. Today it means any period of enforced isolation that keeps an illness from spreading. There is no prefix or suffix to peel off; the whole word still counts out those forty days at anchor.

Use the root in a new word: quarter

Use the root in a new word: quarter: A quarter is one of four equal parts — the same Latin root for 'four' that grew into quaranta, 'forty,' the forty-day wait hiding inside quarantine.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / medical

Quarantine is a formal, specific term for medical isolation to prevent disease spread. Use it when health authority and disease prevention are key. For general separation or isolation, the plainer word 'isolate' is more natural.
